```
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when the required content genuinely needs more space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via the sync procedure there; re-apply or retire the logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

</system-reminder>

Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

</system-reminder>

1	/**
2	 * Shifts: the durable driver of an unattended fleet. Each district opens a
3	 * slot on its cadence, freezes the plan the slot runs into a content digest,
4	 * and records the whole shift as `shift/*` events in the slot's own session —
5	 * the ledger a restarted process reads to resume exactly the cells that never
6	 * started. Refusals are as durable as runs: a slot arriving over a running
7	 * shift, or one whose district already spent its window, leaves a session
8	 * holding one `shift/skipped`. Nothing here calls a model. The
9	 * [village-shifts Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-village-shifts.md)
10	 * owns the design rationale.
11	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-shifts
12	 */

70	/** Stable error codes of a refused deployment or a slot that cannot be frozen. */
71	export type ShiftErrorCode = 'SHIFT_INVALID_CONFIG' | 'SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN'
72	
73	/** Error returned by the shift boundary for a deployment or slot that cannot run. */
74	export class ShiftError extends HarnessError {
75	  /**
76	   * @param message - human-readable reason.
77	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
78	   */
79	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
80	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
81	  constructor(message: string, code: ShiftErrorCode) {
82	    super(message, code)
83	  }
84	}
85	
86	/** Deployment choices of the shift driver, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
87	export interface Config {
88	  /** Existing absolute directory the fleet mints each cell's workspace under. */
89	  workspaceRoot: string
90	  /** The districts this process drives; at least one, each named once. */
91	  districts: ShiftDistrictConfig[]
92	  /** Whether a district with no slot in the ledger opens one as the process starts. */
93	  startImmediately: boolean
94	}
95	
96	/** The environment selection and the token sums one resume scan produced. */
97	interface ShiftScan {
98	  /** Every shift session's ledger, finished or not. */
99	  readonly ledgers: readonly ShiftLedger[]
100	  /** Every grouped `environment/run` stamp, with the tokens its session accounts for. */
101	  readonly stamped: readonly StampedCell[]
102	}
103	
104	/** Fold `shift/cell` records of one session into counts per outcome. */
105	function countCells(records: readonly ShiftCellRecord[]): ShiftCellCounts {
106	  return {
107	    reported: records.filter(record => record.outcome.kind === 'reported').length,
108	    error: records.filter(record => record.outcome.kind === 'error').length,
109	    interrupted: records.filter(record => record.outcome.kind === 'interrupted').length,
110	  }
111	}
112	
113	/**
114	 * How a finished fleet run ends its shift, read from the records the run left
115	 * in the ledger rather than from the report, so the closing record and the
116	 * cells it counts come from one source.
117	 */
118	function endOutcome(aborted: boolean, ceilingReached: boolean): ShiftEndOutcome {
119	  if (aborted) return 'stopped'
120	  return ceilingReached ? 'ceiling' : 'completed'
121	}
122	
123	/** Shifts (`ctx.shifts`): a cadenced, spend-windowed, resumable loop over fleet plans. */
124	export class ShiftService extends Service {
125	  static inject = ['fleet', 'sessions', 'sessionPersistence']
126	
127	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
128	    workspaceRoot: z.string().required(),
129	    districts: z.array(z.object({
130	      district: z.string().required(),
131	      plan: z.object({
132	        // Branded ids and the merge-extensible kind union have no schemastery
133	        // primitive; the registry rejects an id or kind it does not hold when
134	        // the slot freezes.
135	        environments: z.union([
136	          z.object({ ids: z.array(z.string()).required() }),
137	          z.object({ filter: z.object({ kind: z.string() as z<EnvironmentFilter['kind']>, heldOut: z.boolean() }) }),
138	        ]).required() as z<FleetEnvironmentSelection>,
139	        models: z.array(z.object({
140	          provider: z.string().required(),
141	          model: z.string().required(),
142	        })).required(),
143	        repetitions: z.natural().min(1).required(),
144	        tokenCeiling: z.natural().min(1),
145	      }).required(),
146	      cadence: z.object({
147	        intervalMs: z.natural().min(1).required(),
148	      }).required(),
149	      // Prevent Schemastery from materializing an omitted spendWindow as `{}`,
150	      // whose missing fields would reject every district that runs uncapped.
151	      spendWindow: z.object({
152	        windowMs: z.natural().min(1).required(),
153	        maxTokens: z.natural().min(1).required(),
154	      }).default(undefined as unknown as ShiftSpendWindowConfig),
155	    })).required(),
156	    startImmediately: z.boolean().required(),
157	  })
158	
159	  private readonly config: Config
160	  /** The single run of the loop; a second `start()` joins the first. */
161	  private opening: Promise<void> | undefined
162	  /** District to the slot it is running, so a slot over a running shift is refused. */
163	  private readonly running = new Map<string, Promise<void>>()
164	  /** District to the disposer of its armed cadence timer. */
165	  private readonly timers = new Map<string, () => unknown>()
166	  /** Cancellation of the fleet run in flight, absent between runs. */
167	  private controller: AbortController | undefined
168	  private stopping = false
169	
170	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
171	    super(ctx, 'shifts')
172	    this.config = config
173	    if (!isAbsolute(config.workspaceRoot) || !isDirectory(config.workspaceRoot)) {
174	      throw new ShiftError(`workspaceRoot "${config.workspaceRoot}" is not an existing absolute directory`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_CONFIG')
175	    }
176	    if (config.districts.length === 0) throw new ShiftError('the driver is composed with no district', 'SHIFT_INVALID_CONFIG')
177	    const named = new Set<string>()
178	    for (const district of config.districts) {
179	      if (named.has(district.district)) {
180	        throw new ShiftError(`district "${district.district}" is configured twice`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_CONFIG')
181	      }
182	      named.add(district.district)
183	      if (district.plan.models.length === 0) {
184	        throw new ShiftError(`district "${district.district}" names no model route`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_CONFIG')
185	      }
186	    }
187	    ctx.effect(() => () => this.stop(), 'shifts.driver()')
188	    void this.boot()
189	  }
190	
191	  /**
192	   * Resume every interrupted shift, then open each district's due slot and arm
193	   * its cadence timer. The loop runs once per process: a second call joins the
194	   * first, so the plugin's own start and a driver awaiting the first slot
195	   * observe the same run.
196	   * @returns a promise settling once every resumed shift has ended and every
197	   *   district is either running its due slot or armed for its next one.
198	   */
199	  async start(): Promise<void> {
200	    this.opening ??= this.open()
201	    await this.opening
202	  }
203	
204	  /**
205	   * Stop the loop: disarm every cadence timer, cancel the fleet run in flight
206	   * through its signal, and wait for the slots that are settling. The
207	   * interrupted cells end as the runner ends them and their sessions become
208	   * the orphans the next process records.
209	   * @returns a promise settling once no slot is in flight.
210	   */
211	  async stop(): Promise<void> {
212	    this.stopping = true
213	    this.controller?.abort(new Error('the shift driver is stopping'))
214	    for (const disarm of this.timers.values()) await disarm()
215	    this.timers.clear()
216	    await Promise.allSettled([...this.running.values()])
217	  }
218	
219	  /** Start the loop over a settled application; a failure leaves the process running and logged. */
220	  private async boot(): Promise<void> {
221	    try {
222	      // A slot freezes its plan against the environment registry, which sibling
223	      // Loader entries fill; a hand-built tree has no Loader and is settled already.
224	      await this.ctx.get('loader')?.await()
225	      await this.start()
226	    } catch (error: unknown) {
227	      this.ctx.logger.error(`the shift driver did not start: ${String(error)}`)
228	    }
229	  }
230	
231	  /** One pass of resume and district opening. */
232	  private async open(): Promise<void> {
233	    const scan = await this.scan()
234	    for (const ledger of scan.ledgers) {
235	      if (this.stopping) return
236	      if (ledger.end === undefined) await this.resume(ledger, scan.stamped)
237	    }
238	    for (const district of this.config.districts) {
239	      if (this.stopping) return
240	      await this.openDistrict(district, previousSlot(scan.ledgers, district.district))
241	    }
242	  }
243	
244	  /** Arm the district's cadence, then run the slot it already owes. */
245	  private async openDistrict(district: ShiftDistrictConfig, previous: number | undefined): Promise<void> {
246	    const at = nextSlotAt(previous, district.cadence.intervalMs, Date.now(), this.config.startImmediately)
247	    if (at > Date.now()) {
248	      this.arm(district, at)
249	      return
250	    }
251	    this.arm(district, nextSlotAt(at, district.cadence.intervalMs, Date.now(), false))
252	    await this.slot(district, at)
253	  }
254	
255	  /**
256	   * Replace one district's cadence timer with one firing at `at`. Each firing
257	   * arms the next slot before it runs this one, so slots keep arriving on the
258	   * cadence and a slot that lands on a still-running shift is refused rather
259	   * than delayed into it.
260	   */
261	  private arm(district: ShiftDistrictConfig, at: number): void {
262	    void this.timers.get(district.district)?.()
263	    const disarm = this.ctx.effect(() => {
264	      const timer = setTimeout(() => {
265	        this.arm(district, nextSlotAt(at, district.cadence.intervalMs, Date.now(), false))
266	        // A slot that cannot be frozen must not take the loop down with it: the
267	        // next slot is already armed and the failure is the operator's signal.
268	        void this.slot(district, at).catch((error: unknown) => {
269	          this.ctx.logger.error(`district "${district.district}" slot ${at} failed: ${String(error)}`)
270	        })
271	      }, Math.max(0, at - Date.now()))
272	      return () => {
273	        clearTimeout(timer)
274	      }
275	    }, `shifts.cadence(${district.district})`)
276	    this.timers.set(district.district, disarm)
277	  }
278	
279	  /** Freeze one slot and either refuse it or run it, keeping one shift per district in flight. */
280	  private async slot(district: ShiftDistrictConfig, scheduledAt: number): Promise<void> {
281	    const plan = this.freeze(district)
282	    const digest = shiftDigest(plan)
283	    const id = shiftId(digest, scheduledAt)
284	    if (this.running.has(plan.district)) {
285	      await this.skip(id, { digest, scheduledAt, reason: 'overlap' })
286	      return
287	    }
288	    const inFlight = this.runSlot(district, plan, digest, id, scheduledAt)
289	      .finally(() => {
290	        this.running.delete(plan.district)
291	      })
292	    this.running.set(plan.district, inFlight)
293	    await inFlight
294	  }
295	
296	  /** Refuse the slot for its district's spend window, or open the shift and drive it. */
297	  private async runSlot(
298	    district: ShiftDistrictConfig,
299	    plan: ShiftPlan,
300	    digest: string,
301	    id: string,
302	    scheduledAt: number,
303	  ): Promise<void> {
304	    const window = district.spendWindow
305	    if (window !== undefined) {
306	      const scan = await this.scan()
307	      const spent = windowSpend(scan.ledgers, plan.district, window.windowMs, Date.now())
308	      if (spent >= window.maxTokens) {
309	        await this.skip(id, { digest, scheduledAt, reason: 'spend-window' })
310	        return
311	      }
312	    }
313	    const cells = shiftCells(plan)
314	    const session = this.ctx.sessions.prepare(SessionId(id), { meta: { cwd: this.config.workspaceRoot } })
315	    await this.publish(session, async () => {
316	      session.append('shift/start', { shiftId: id, digest, plan, scheduledAt })
317	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
318	      await this.drive(session, id, plan, cells, 0)
319	    })
320	  }
321	
322	  /** Record one refused slot as its own session, holding that one event. */
323	  private async skip(id: string, skipped: ShiftSkipped): Promise<void> {
324	    const session = this.ctx.sessions.prepare(SessionId(id), { meta: { cwd: this.config.workspaceRoot } })
325	    await this.publish(session, () => {
326	      session.append('shift/skipped', skipped)
327	    })
328	  }
329	
330	  /** Record the orphans of an interrupted process, then run what never started. */
331	  private async resume(ledger: ShiftLedger, stamped: readonly StampedCell[]): Promise<void> {
332	    const { plan, shiftId: id } = ledger.start
333	    const cells = shiftCells(plan)
334	    const split = splitPending(cells, ledger, stamped)
335	    const preparation = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.prepare(ledger.sessionId)
336	    const { session } = preparation
337	    try {
338	      await this.publish(session, async () => {
339	        for (const orphan of split.orphans) {
340	          session.append('shift/cell', {
341	            shiftId: id,
342	            cell: orphan.cell,
343	            sessionId: orphan.sessionId,
344	            outcome: { kind: 'interrupted' },
345	          })
346	        }
347	        session.append('shift/resume', { shiftId: id, done: split.done, pending: split.pending })
348	        await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
349	        await this.drive(session, id, plan, split.pending, shiftSpend(stamped, id))
350	      })
351	    } finally {
352	      preparation[Symbol.dispose]()
353	    }
354	  }
355	
356	  /**
357	   * Run the pending cells of one shift through the fleet, writing one
358	   * `shift/cell` per announced cell, and close the ledger.
359	   */
360	  private async drive(
361	    session: Session,
362	    id: string,
363	    plan: ShiftPlan,
364	    pending: readonly FleetCell[],
365	    spent: number,
366	  ): Promise<void> {
367	    if (pending.length === 0) {
368	      await this.close(session, id, 'completed', 0)
369	      return
370	    }
371	    const remaining = plan.tokenCeiling === undefined ? undefined : plan.tokenCeiling - spent
372	    if (remaining !== undefined && remaining < 1) {
373	      await this.close(session, id, 'ceiling', 0)
374	      return
375	    }
376	    const controller = new AbortController()
377	    this.controller = controller
378	    let ceilingReached = false
379	    // The fleet announces a cell after its session is durable and its
380	    // workspace reaped, so the ledger entry only ever follows the fact.
381	    const unobserve = this.ctx.on('fleet/cell', (payload) => {
382	      if (payload.group !== id) return
383	      if (payload.outcome.kind === 'error' && payload.outcome.code === 'FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED') ceilingReached = true
384	      session.append('shift/cell', {
385	        shiftId: id,
386	        cell: payload.cell,
387	        ...payload.outcome.kind === 'reported' ? { sessionId: payload.outcome.sessionId } : {},
388	        outcome: payload.outcome.kind === 'reported'
389	          ? { kind: 'reported', certified: payload.outcome.certified }
390	          : { kind: 'error', ...payload.outcome.code === undefined ? {} : { code: payload.outcome.code }, message: payload.outcome.message },
391	      })
392	    })
393	    let report: FleetRunReport
394	    try {
395	      report = await this.ctx.fleet.run({
396	        environments: { ids: plan.environments },
397	        models: plan.models,
398	        repetitions: plan.repetitions,
399	        cells: pending,
400	        workspaceRoot: this.config.workspaceRoot,
401	        group: id,
402	        district: plan.district,
403	        ...remaining === undefined ? {} : { tokenCeiling: remaining },
404	        signal: controller.signal,
405	      })
406	    } finally {
407	      unobserve()
408	      this.controller = undefined
409	    }
410	    const outcome = endOutcome(controller.signal.aborted, ceilingReached)
411	    await this.close(session, id, outcome, report.spend.inputTokens + report.spend.outputTokens)
412	  }
413	
414	  /** Append the closing record over every cell the session holds and flush it. */
415	  private async close(session: Session, id: string, outcome: ShiftEndOutcome, spend: number): Promise<void> {
416	    const records = session.events.flatMap(event => (event.type === 'shift/cell' ? [event.data] : []))
417	    session.append('shift/end', { shiftId: id, outcome, spend, cells: countCells(records) })
418	    await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
419	  }
420	
421	  /**
422	   * Publish one slot session for the length of the slot, flush it, and detach.
423	   * The entry is owned by this fiber, so a disposal that races a slot removes
424	   * it after {@link ShiftService.stop} has let the slot settle.
425	   */
426	  private async publish(session: Session, body: () => Promise<void> | void): Promise<void> {
427	    const detach = this.ctx.effect(function* (this: ShiftService) {
428	      yield this.ctx.sessions.enter(session)
429	      this.ctx.sessions.announce(session)
430	    }.bind(this), `shifts.slot(${session.id})`)
431	    try {
432	      await body()
433	    } finally {
434	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
435	      await detach()
436	    }
437	  }
438	
439	  /** Read every persisted session once: the shift ledgers and the grouped run stamps. */
440	  private async scan(): Promise<ShiftScan> {
441	    const ledgers: ShiftLedger[] = []
442	    const stamped: StampedCell[] = []
443	    for (const header of await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.list()) {
444	      const inspection = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect(header.id)
445	      const scanned = { meta: inspection.meta, events: inspection.events }
446	      const ledger = foldShiftLedger(scanned)
447	      if (ledger !== undefined) ledgers.push(ledger)
448	      stamped.push(...stampedCells(scanned, foldBudgetSpend(inspection.events, {}).totalTokens))
449	    }
450	    return { ledgers, stamped }
451	  }
452	
453	  /** Resolve one district's environment selection against the registry and freeze its plan. */
454	  private freeze(district: ShiftDistrictConfig): ShiftPlan {
455	    const environments = this.select(district.district, district.plan.environments)
456	    if (environments.length === 0) {
457	      throw new ShiftError(`district "${district.district}" selects no environment`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN')
458	    }
459	    return {
460	      district: district.district,
461	      environments,
462	      models: district.plan.models,
463	      repetitions: district.plan.repetitions,
464	      ...district.plan.tokenCeiling === undefined ? {} : { tokenCeiling: district.plan.tokenCeiling },
465	    }
466	  }
467	
468	  /** The environment ids one selection names, in registry order for a filter. */
469	  private select(district: string, selection: FleetEnvironmentSelection): EnvironmentId[] {
470	    // The fleet declares the registry injection this driver reads through; a
471	    // composition without it cannot run a cell at all.
472	    const registry = this.ctx.get('environments')
473	    if (registry === undefined) {
474	      throw new ShiftError(`district "${district}" cannot freeze a plan without the environment registry`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN')
475	    }
476	    if ('ids' in selection) {
477	      return selection.ids.map((id) => {
478	        if (registry.get(id) === undefined) {
479	          throw new ShiftError(`environment "${id}" of district "${district}" is not registered`, 'SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN')
480	        }
481	        return id
482	      })
483	    }
484	    return registry.list(selection.filter).map(definition => definition.id)
485	  }
486	}
487	
488	/** Directory test that treats a missing or unreadable path as no directory. */
489	function isDirectory(path: string): boolean {
490	  try {
491	    return statSync(path).isDirectory()
492	  } catch {
493	    // statSync throws for a missing or unreadable path; both mean the
494	    // deployment named no usable workspace root.
495	    return false
496	  }
497	}
498	
499	export default ShiftService

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of the shift driver: the frozen plan, the five `shift/*` events
3	 * one shift session carries, and the deployment records the config validates
4	 * into, free of host-side imports.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-shifts/types
7	 */
8	
9	import type { EnvironmentId, EnvironmentRunModel } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
10	import type { FleetCell, FleetEnvironmentSelection } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet/types'
11	import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
12	
13	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
14	  interface SessionEventMap {
15	    /**
16	     * Opening record of one shift: the identity the slot froze, the digest its
17	     * plan hashes to, the frozen plan verbatim, and the slot time the cadence
18	     * computed. Appended once, before the shift's first cell starts, and the
19	     * only event that tells a later process a shift exists to resume.
20	     */
21	    'shift/start': ShiftStart
22	    /**
23	     * One cell of the shift settled: the cell's coordinates, the session the
24	     * runner created for it when one exists, and its outcome. Appended once
25	     * per cell, after the cell's own session is durable — including for an
26	     * orphan a later process found stamped but unrecorded, which it records as
27	     * `interrupted` and never runs again.
28	     */
29	    'shift/cell': ShiftCellRecord
30	    /**
31	     * A later process picked this shift up: the cells already settled and the
32	     * cells this process runs. Appended after the orphans of the interrupted
33	     * process are recorded and before the pending cells start.
34	     */
35	    'shift/resume': ShiftResume
36	    /**
37	     * The slot was refused and no shift started: the plan digest and slot time
38	     * that were refused, and why. It is the only event of its session, so a
39	     * refused slot is as durable as a run one.
40	     */
41	    'shift/skipped': ShiftSkipped
42	    /**
43	     * Closing record of one shift: how it ended, the tokens this process's
44	     * cells spent, and the cell counts per outcome. Its presence is what marks
45	     * the shift finished, so a session with `shift/start` and no `shift/end`
46	     * is exactly what a later process resumes.
47	     */
48	    'shift/end': ShiftEnd
49	  }
50	}
51	
52	/**
53	 * One shift's frozen plan. `environments` holds the ids a config filter
54	 * resolved to against the registry at freeze time, so the digest and the cell
55	 * enumeration are decided before any cell runs and a registry that changes
56	 * mid-shift cannot move them.
57	 */
58	export interface ShiftPlan {
59	  /** District every cell of the shift is stamped with. */
60	  readonly district: string
61	  /** Environments the shift runs, as resolved at freeze time. */
62	  readonly environments: readonly EnvironmentId[]
63	  /** Model routes in listing order, at least one; the fleet enumerates cells in it. */
64	  readonly models: readonly EnvironmentRunModel[]
65	  /** Positive number of repetitions per environment and route; repetition indexes start at zero. */
66	  readonly repetitions: number
67	  /** Positive integer bound on the input plus output tokens the shift's reported cells may sum to. */
68	  readonly tokenCeiling?: number
69	}
70	
71	/** Payload of `shift/start`. */
72	export interface ShiftStart {
73	  /** `shift-<digest>-<scheduledAt>`, the `group` every cell of this shift is stamped with. */
74	  readonly shiftId: string
75	  /** Content digest of {@link ShiftStart.plan}. */
76	  readonly digest: string
77	  /** The frozen plan, verbatim. */
78	  readonly plan: ShiftPlan
79	  /** Slot time in epoch milliseconds; the cadence counts the next slot from it. */
80	  readonly scheduledAt: number
81	}
82	
83	/**
84	 * What one cell of a shift produced: a report with its certification, the
85	 * failure that prevented one, or the crash that left a started cell with no
86	 * outcome at all.
87	 */
88	export type ShiftCellOutcome =
89	  | { readonly kind: 'reported'; readonly certified: boolean }
90	  | { readonly kind: 'error'; readonly code?: string; readonly message: string }
91	  | { readonly kind: 'interrupted' }
92	
93	/** Payload of `shift/cell`. */
94	export interface ShiftCellRecord {
95	  /** The shift this cell belongs to; it equals the `shift/start` of the same session. */
96	  readonly shiftId: string
97	  /** The environment, model route, and repetition this record settles. */
98	  readonly cell: FleetCell
99	  /** Session the runner created for the cell, absent for a cell that never reached the runner. */
100	  readonly sessionId?: SessionId
101	  readonly outcome: ShiftCellOutcome
102	}
103	
104	/** Payload of `shift/resume`. */
105	export interface ShiftResume {
106	  readonly shiftId: string
107	  /** Cells that will not run again: those already recorded, plus the orphans just recorded. */
108	  readonly done: readonly FleetCell[]
109	  /** Cells this process runs, in plan order. */
110	  readonly pending: readonly FleetCell[]
111	}
112	
113	/** Why a slot was refused before any cell of it existed. */
114	export type ShiftSkipReason = 'overlap' | 'spend-window'
115	
116	/** Payload of `shift/skipped`. */
117	export interface ShiftSkipped {
118	  /** Digest of the plan the refused slot would have run. */
119	  readonly digest: string
120	  /** Slot time in epoch milliseconds the cadence computed for the refused slot. */
121	  readonly scheduledAt: number
122	  readonly reason: ShiftSkipReason
123	}
124	
125	/**
126	 * How a shift ended: `completed` once every pending cell settled, `ceiling`
127	 * when the plan's token ceiling refused the cells that were left, `stopped`
128	 * when the driver was asked to stop and cancelled the run.
129	 */
130	export type ShiftEndOutcome = 'completed' | 'ceiling' | 'stopped'
131	
132	/** Cells of one shift counted by the outcome their `shift/cell` records carry. */
133	export interface ShiftCellCounts {
134	  readonly reported: number
135	  readonly error: number
136	  readonly interrupted: number
137	}
138	
139	/** Payload of `shift/end`. */
140	export interface ShiftEnd {
141	  readonly shiftId: string
142	  readonly outcome: ShiftEndOutcome
143	  /** Input plus output tokens this process's cells reported; the spend window sums it across slots. */
144	  readonly spend: number
145	  /** Counts over every `shift/cell` of the session, this process's and its predecessors'. */
146	  readonly cells: ShiftCellCounts
147	}
148	
149	/** Environments, routes, repetitions, and ceiling one district's slots run. */
150	export interface ShiftPlanConfig {
151	  /** Environments to run: named ids, or everything the registry filter matches at freeze time. */
152	  environments: FleetEnvironmentSelection
153	  /**
154	   * Model routes to run, at least one. The shift enumerates its own cells to
155	   * compute a pending set and to digest the plan, so the routes are named here
156	   * rather than taken from whatever default the composition currently selects.
157	   */
158	  models: EnvironmentRunModel[]
159	  /** Positive number of repetitions per environment and route. */
160	  repetitions: number
161	  /** Positive integer token ceiling of one shift; absent runs each shift uncapped. */
162	  tokenCeiling?: number
163	}
164	
165	/** How often one district opens a slot. */
166	export interface ShiftCadenceConfig {
167	  /** Positive milliseconds between consecutive slots of the district. */
168	  intervalMs: number
169	}
170	
171	/** The spend a district may reach across slots before its next one is refused. */
172	export interface ShiftSpendWindowConfig {
173	  /** Positive width of the trailing window in milliseconds. */
174	  windowMs: number
175	  /** Positive token sum inside the window at which the next slot is refused. */
176	  maxTokens: number
177	}
178	
179	/** One district's shifts: what they run, how often, and what they may spend. */
180	export interface ShiftDistrictConfig {
181	  /** District name, unique in the deployment; every cell's run stamp carries it. */
182	  district: string
183	  /** What every slot of this district runs, frozen into the shift digest. */
184	  plan: ShiftPlanConfig
185	  /** How often the district opens a slot. */
186	  cadence: ShiftCadenceConfig
187	  /** Cross-slot spend ceiling; absent lets the district run every slot its cadence opens. */
188	  spendWindow?: ShiftSpendWindowConfig
189	}

1	/**
2	 * Service Definition for the approval capability seam, covering requests, cancellation, audit, and per-session policy. Missing
3	 * answerers fail closed; grants apply only to the requested action.
4	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-user-approval
5	 */
6	
7	import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto'
8	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
9	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
10	import type { Agent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
11	import { createUserMessage, type CallId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import { scopeTarget } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope'
13	import type { Scoped } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope'
14	import type { Session, SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
15	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt'
16	
17	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
18	  interface Context {
19	    approval: ApprovalService
20	  }
21	
22	  interface Events {
23	    /**
24	     * Ask composed answerers for one decision. Return an outcome to claim the
25	     * request or call `next()`; failure yields the fail-closed default.
26	     * Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): agent-scoped listeners receive only that agent.
27	     * @param req - the pending decision (agent, tool identity, reason, signal).
28	     * @mode waterfall
29	     */
30	    'approval/request'(this: Scoped<ApprovalService>, req: ApprovalRequest, next: () => Promise<ApprovalOutcome>): Promise<ApprovalOutcome>
31	  }
32	}
33	
34	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
35	  interface SessionEventMap {
36	    /**
37	     * An approval question was put to the answerer chain — log-only audit
38	     * (like `hook/*`; NOT a surface event, carries no `surfaceOp`). `id` pairs
39	     * it with the `approval/decided` that always follows; `toolName` is the
40	     * tool the question is about, `callId` the exact tool call when the asker
41	     * had one, `reason` the asker's human-readable explanation (e.g. a hook's
42	     * permission-decision reason).
43	     */
44	    'approval/asked': {
45	      id: ApprovalRequestId
46	      toolName: string
47	      callId?: CallId
48	      reason?: string
49	    }
50	    /**
51	     * The outcome of a prior `approval/asked` (same `id`) — log-only audit.
52	     * Exactly one per ask, appended when the outcome is known: a decision, a
53	     * cancellation, or the fail-closed `'unavailable'`.
54	     */
55	    'approval/decided': {
56	      id: ApprovalRequestId
57	      outcome: ApprovalOutcome
58	    }
59	    /**
60	     * The session's approval policy was switched — log-only, durable,
61	     * replayable, never in the model transcript (the model learns the policy
62	     * from the runtime-context snapshot and live switch notices). The LAST
63	     * such event is the session's override ({@link effectiveApprovalPolicy}).
64	     * `source: 'delegation'` marks an override seeded into a child; an absent
65	     * source is a runtime switch.
66	     */
67	    'approval/policy': {
68	      policy: ApprovalPolicy
69	      /** Marks an override seeded into a child at delegation. */
70	      source?: 'delegation'
71	    }
72	  }
73	}
74	
75	import { ApprovalRequestId } from './types.ts'
76	import type { ApprovalOutcome } from './types.ts'
77	
78	export { ApprovalRequestId } from './types.ts'
79	export type { ApprovalOutcome } from './types.ts'
80	
81	/** Every {@link ApprovalOutcome}, for runtime normalization of answerer returns. */
82	const OUTCOMES: readonly ApprovalOutcome[] = ['allowed-once', 'rejected', 'cancelled', 'unavailable']
83	
84	/**
85	 * A session's approval policy — what happens to an {@link ApprovalService}
86	 * ask BEFORE any interactive answerer sees it:
87	 *
88	 * - `'ask'` (the default) — delegate to the composed answerers; with none
89	 *   composed the chain falls through to the fail-closed `'unavailable'`.
90	 * - `'never'` — never prompt anyone: every ask resolves `'rejected'`
91	 *   deterministically. The strict headless stance (CI, unattended runs) and
92	 *   the policy whose outcome is knowable without asking.
93	 */
94	export type ApprovalPolicy = 'ask' | 'never'
95	
96	/** Every {@link ApprovalPolicy}, for option advertisement and runtime validation of untrusted policy strings. */
97	export const APPROVAL_POLICIES: readonly ApprovalPolicy[] = ['ask', 'never']
98	
99	/** Model-facing statement for the deterministic `'never'` policy. */
100	const NEVER_SENTENCE = 'Approval prompts are disabled in this session: actions that require approval are rejected automatically — do not request sandbox escalation (do not set `sandbox_permissions`).'
101	/** Model-facing statement for an interactive policy that may still fail closed. */
102	const ASK_SENTENCE = 'Approval policy: ask. Operations that require approval may ask through the configured answerers; without an available answerer, the request fails closed.'
103	
104	/**
105	 * The session's approval-policy override: the last `approval/policy` event in
106	 * the log, or undefined when the session never switched (callers apply the
107	 * plugin's configured default). The pure fold — resume needs no catch-up
108	 * machinery because replaying the log IS the state.
109	 * @param events - session events in log order (other event types are skipped).
110	 * @returns the policy of the last switch event, or undefined without one.
111	 */
112	export function effectiveApprovalPolicy(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): ApprovalPolicy | undefined {
113	  for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
114	    const event = events[index] as SessionEvent
115	    if (event.type === 'approval/policy') return event.data.policy
116	  }
117	  return undefined
118	}
119	
120	/**
121	 * Whether the log currently sits inside an open turn (a `turn/start` not yet
122	 * closed by a `turn/end`) — the {@link ApprovalService.request} precondition.
123	 * The audit pair must be turn-enclosed: the turn is the durable log's
124	 * commit/replay boundary, so a bare event appended between turns is
125	 * indistinguishable from a crash tail and silently dropped on reload.
126	 */
127	function hasOpenTurn(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): boolean {
128	  for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
129	    const type = (events[index] as SessionEvent).type
130	    if (type === 'turn/start') return true
131	    if (type === 'turn/end') return false
132	  }
133	  return false
134	}
135	
136	/**
137	 * Append the sole durable representation of a session policy override. Invalid
138	 * values throw before the log changes; consumers fold the new value on each read.
139	 * @param session - the session the override belongs to.
140	 * @param policy - the policy in effect until the next switch.
141	 */
142	export function setApprovalPolicy(session: Session, policy: ApprovalPolicy): void {
143	  if (!APPROVAL_POLICIES.includes(policy)) {
144	    throw new TypeError('approval policy must be one of "ask" or "never"')
145	  }
146	  session.append('approval/policy', { policy })
147	}
148	
149	/**
150	 * Readonly same-process permission question. `callId` links to an already
151	 * presented tool call, so arguments are not duplicated here.
152	 */
153	export interface ApprovalRequest {
154	  /**
155	   * The agent on whose behalf the question is asked. Routes the question (a
156	   * UI answerer only answers for agents it owns) and receives the audit
157	   * events on its session log.
158	   */
159	  readonly agent: Agent
160	  /** The tool the question is about (presentation and audit). */
161	  readonly toolName: string
162	  /**
163	   * The exact tool call being decided, when the asker has one — lets a UI
164	   * attach the prompt to the tool call it already streamed.
165	   */
166	  readonly callId?: CallId
167	  /** The asker's human-readable explanation of WHY it is asking. */
168	  readonly reason?: string
169	  /**
170	   * Aborting withdraws the question: the request settles `'cancelled'`
171	   * immediately and a late answer from a still-pending answerer is discarded.
172	   */
173	  readonly signal?: AbortSignal
174	}
175	
176	/** Plugin config. All optional — `static Config` supplies the defaults. */
177	export interface Config {
178	  /**
179	   * The deployment's default {@link ApprovalPolicy} for sessions without an
180	   * `approval/policy` override — `'ask'` delegates to the composed answerers
181	   * (fail-closed with none); `'never'` auto-rejects every ask without
182	   * prompting (the deterministic CI/unattended stance).
183	   */
184	  readonly policy?: ApprovalPolicy
185	}
186	
187	/**
188	 * Approval service that applies session policy before answerers and logs every
189	 * ask/outcome pair to the requesting session. It exposes deterministic policy
190	 * changes to the model through the runtime-context snapshot and switch notices.
191	 */
192	export class ApprovalService extends Service {
193	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
194	    policy: z.union(['ask', 'never'] as const).default('ask'),
195	  })
196	
197	  constructor(ctx: Context, public config: Config) {
198	    super(ctx, 'approval')
199	
200	    const effective = (agent: Agent): ApprovalPolicy => this.effectivePolicy(agent.session)
201	
202	    // The complete current value travels after retained history, so switching
203	    // policy does not rewrite the stable system-prompt cache prefix.
204	    ctx.inject(['systemPrompt'], (scope: Context) => {
205	      scope.systemPrompt.context({
206	        name: 'approval:policy',
207	        order: 115,
208	        text: (context) => {
209	          const agent = context.agent
210	          // A bare assemble() (tests, diagnostics) has no session to state.
211	          if (agent === undefined) return ''
212	          const policy = effective(agent)
213	          return policy === 'never' ? NEVER_SENTENCE : ASK_SENTENCE
214	        },
215	      })
216	    })
217	  }
218	
219	  /**
220	   * Switch one live agent's policy and queue the transition for its next model
221	   * step. Session initialization uses {@link setApprovalPolicy} directly
222	   * because there is no previously visible policy to change.
223	   * @param agent - the live agent whose policy is changing.
224	   * @param policy - the new effective policy.
225	   */
226	  setPolicy(agent: Agent, policy: ApprovalPolicy): void {
227	    const previous = this.effectivePolicy(agent.session)
228	    if (previous === policy) return
229	    setApprovalPolicy(agent.session, policy)
230	    agent.inject(createUserMessage({
231	      content: [{
232	        type: 'text',
233	        text: `The approval policy changed from "${previous}" to "${policy}" (changed by the user).`,
234	      }],
235	      source: { kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'user-approval' },
236	    }))
237	  }
238	
239	  /**
240	   * Ask the composed answerers to decide one readonly same-process request.
241	   * The service borrows the request, agent, session, and live signal directly.
242	   * The request requires an open turn because the audit pair must be enclosed
243	   * by the durable log's commit/replay boundary; an idle ask rejects before
244	   * appending anything. The answerer phase always produces an outcome: an
245	   * aborted signal yields `'cancelled'`, a missing or throwing answerer yields
246	   * `'unavailable'` (fail closed), and a rogue non-vocabulary return value is
247	   * normalized to `'unavailable'`. A failure that prevents either audit append
248	   * from committing still rejects because returning an unlogged decision would
249	   * violate the pair. Session contains post-commit observer failures, so an
250	   * authoritative append cannot reject the request or suppress its matching
251	   * audit event.
252	   * @param req - the pending decision (agent, tool identity, reason, signal).
253	   * @returns the closed outcome; `'allowed-once'` is the only grant.
254	   * @throws when no turn is open or either audit event fails before the session
255	   *   append commit point.
256	   */
257	  async request(req: ApprovalRequest): Promise<ApprovalOutcome> {
258	    const session = req.agent.session
259	    if (!hasOpenTurn(session.events)) {
260	      throw new Error(
261	        'approval.request() outside an open turn: the approval/asked + approval/decided audit pair '
262	        + 'must be turn-enclosed (a bare event between turns is crash-tail garbage on reload). '
263	        + 'Ask from inside the turn that needs the decision.',
264	      )
265	    }
266	    const id = ApprovalRequestId(randomUUID())
267	    session.append('approval/asked', {
268	      id,
269	      toolName: req.toolName,
270	      ...req.callId !== undefined ? { callId: req.callId } : {},
271	      ...req.reason !== undefined ? { reason: req.reason } : {},
272	    })
273	    const outcome = await this.decide(req, session)
274	    session.append('approval/decided', { id, outcome })
275	    return outcome
276	  }
277	
278	  /**
279	   * The session's effective policy: its own `approval/policy` fold, else the
280	   * configured default (the schema already defaulted an omitted policy to
281	   * `'ask'`; the `??` only narrows the optional-input TYPE).
282	   * @param session - the exact accepted session whose policy applies.
283	   * @returns the policy every ask for this session resolves under right now.
284	   */
285	  private effectivePolicy(session: Session): ApprovalPolicy {
286	    return this.overrideOf(session) ?? this.config.policy ?? 'ask'
287	  }
288	
289	  /**
290	   * Read the session override without applying the configured default.
291	   * @param session - session whose log supplies the override.
292	   * @returns the last logged policy, or `undefined` without one.
293	   */
294	  overrideOf(session: Session): ApprovalPolicy | undefined {
295	    return effectiveApprovalPolicy(session.events)
296	  }
297	
298	  /**
299	   * Dispatch the waterfall, contained and raced against the request signal.
300	   * @param req - the borrowed public request.
301	   * @param session - the request agent's session used for policy lookup.
302	   * @returns the normalized closed outcome.
303	   */
304	  private async decide(req: ApprovalRequest, session: Session): Promise<ApprovalOutcome> {
305	    const signal = req.signal
306	    if (signal?.aborted) return 'cancelled'
307	    // The 'never' policy is decided HERE, before any dispatch: a listener
308	    // registered with `prepend: true` after this service mounts would sit
309	    // ahead of any gate LISTENER, so a listener-shaped gate cannot keep the
310	    // documented promise that 'never' rejects deterministically regardless
311	    // of registration order — only the service's own request path can.
312	    if (this.effectivePolicy(session) === 'never') return 'rejected'
313	    // Enter the promise chain BEFORE dispatching: a listener that throws
314	    // SYNCHRONOUSLY (before its first await) must land in the same rejection
315	    // path as an async one — `Promise.resolve(call())` would let it escape
316	    // the containment into the caller.
317	    const answer: Promise<ApprovalOutcome> = Promise.resolve().then(
318	      () => this.ctx.waterfall(
319	        scopeTarget(this, req.agent), 'approval/request', req,
320	        () => Promise.resolve<ApprovalOutcome>('unavailable'),
321	      ),
322	    ).then(
323	      // Normalize a rogue (non-vocabulary) answerer return to the fail-closed
324	      // outcome instead of leaking it into callers' closed-union switches.
325	      outcome => OUTCOMES.includes(outcome) ? outcome : 'unavailable',
326	      // A throwing answerer must fail the QUESTION closed, not the caller's
327	      // tool call open — the seam contains its callbacks.
328	      () => 'unavailable',
329	    )
330	    if (signal === undefined) return answer
331	    return await new Promise<ApprovalOutcome>((resolve) => {
332	      const onAbort = () => {
333	        signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort)
334	        resolve('cancelled')
335	      }
336	      signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true })
337	      void answer.then((outcome) => {
338	        signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort)
339	        // After an abort won the race this resolve is a settled-promise no-op:
340	        // the late answer is discarded by construction.
341	        resolve(outcome)
342	      })
343	    })
344	  }
345	}

1	/** Package-owned approval audit-stream invariants. @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-user-approval/invariant */
2	
3	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
4	import type { Session, SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
5	import type { InvariantFailure, InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
6	import type { ApprovalRequestId } from './index.ts'
7	import { APPROVAL_POLICIES } from './index.ts'
8	
9	const PACKAGE_NAME = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-user-approval'
10	const APPROVAL_OUTCOMES = ['allowed-once', 'rejected', 'cancelled', 'unavailable'] as const
11	
12	/** Cordis companion plugin name. */
13	export const name = 'user-approval-invariant'
14	/** Service required before the companion can reserve package ownership. */
15	export const inject = ['invariants']
16	
17	type ApprovalTransition =
18	  | { kind: 'asked'; id: ApprovalRequestId }
19	  | { kind: 'decided'; id: ApprovalRequestId }
20	
21	interface ApprovalTrace {
22	  openTurn: number | null
23	  pending: Set<ApprovalRequestId>
24	}
25	
26	/** Validate one approval event against committed unmatched questions. */
27	function validateApprovalEvent(
28	  trace: ApprovalTrace,
29	  event: SessionEvent,
30	  fail: InvariantFailure,
31	): ApprovalTransition | undefined {
32	  if (event.type === 'approval/asked') {
33	    if (trace.openTurn === null) fail('approval/asked appended outside any open turn')
34	    if (event.data.toolName.length === 0) fail('approval/asked toolName must be non-empty')
35	    if (trace.pending.has(event.data.id)) fail(`approval/asked repeated open id ${JSON.stringify(event.data.id)}`)
36	    return { kind: 'asked', id: event.data.id }
37	  }
38	  if (event.type === 'approval/decided') {
39	    if (trace.openTurn === null) fail('approval/decided appended outside any open turn')
40	    if (!trace.pending.has(event.data.id)) fail(`approval/decided has no matching approval/asked for id ${JSON.stringify(event.data.id)}`)
41	    if (!APPROVAL_OUTCOMES.includes(event.data.outcome)) {
42	      fail(`approval/decided carries unknown outcome ${JSON.stringify(event.data.outcome)}`)
43	    }
44	    return { kind: 'decided', id: event.data.id }
45	  }
46	  if (event.type === 'approval/policy' && !APPROVAL_POLICIES.includes(event.data.policy)) {
47	    fail(`approval/policy carries unknown policy ${JSON.stringify(event.data.policy)}`)
48	  }
49	  return undefined
50	}
51	
52	/** Apply one accepted approval-pair transition. */
53	function applyApprovalTransition(pending: Set<ApprovalRequestId>, transition: ApprovalTransition): void {
54	  if (transition.kind === 'asked') pending.add(transition.id)
55	  else pending.delete(transition.id)
56	}
57	
58	/** Install audit pairing and closed-vocabulary checks. */
59	// Event owners keep precommit staging local so their vocabularies never move into a central helper.
60	/* jscpd:ignore-start */
61	const install: InvariantInstaller = Object.assign((ctx: Context, fail: InvariantFailure) => {
62	  const traces = new WeakMap<Session, ApprovalTrace>()
63	  const staged = new WeakMap<SessionEvent, { session: Session; transition: ApprovalTransition }>()
64	  const seed = (session: Session): ApprovalTrace => {
65	    const trace: ApprovalTrace = { openTurn: null, pending: new Set() }
66	    traces.set(session, trace)
67	    for (const event of session.events) {
68	      if (event.type === 'turn/start') trace.openTurn = event.data.turn
69	      else if (event.type === 'turn/end') trace.openTurn = null
70	      const transition = validateApprovalEvent(trace, event, fail)
71	      if (transition !== undefined) applyApprovalTransition(trace.pending, transition)
72	    }
73	    return trace
74	  }
75	  const traceFor = (session: Session): ApprovalTrace => traces.get(session) ?? seed(session)
76	
77	  for (const session of ctx.sessions.list()) seed(session)
78	  ctx.on('session/created', (session) => { seed(session) }, { global: true })
79	  ctx.on('session/event', (session, event) => {
80	    const trace = traceFor(session)
81	    if (event.type === 'turn/start') {
82	      trace.openTurn = event.data.turn
83	      return
84	    }
85	    if (event.type === 'turn/end') {
86	      trace.openTurn = null
87	      return
88	    }
89	    if (event.type !== 'approval/asked' && event.type !== 'approval/decided') return
90	    const candidate = staged.get(event)
91	    /* v8 ignore next -- internal/dispatch stages every package-owned pair event */
92	    if (candidate === undefined || candidate.session !== session) return fail('approval audit event published without pre-commit validation')
93	    staged.delete(event)
94	    applyApprovalTransition(trace.pending, candidate.transition)
95	  }, { global: true })
96	  ctx.on('internal/dispatch', (_mode, eventName, args) => {
97	    if (eventName !== 'session/event') return
98	    const [session, event] = args as [Session, SessionEvent]
99	    const transition = validateApprovalEvent(traceFor(session), event, fail)
100	    if (transition !== undefined) staged.set(event, { session, transition })
101	  }, { global: true })
102	}, { inject: ['sessions'] })
103	/* jscpd:ignore-end */
104	
105	/**
106	 * Register the approval invariant companion.
107	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the invariant service.
108	 * @returns the installed registration's disposer after setup succeeds.
109	 */
110	export const apply = (ctx: Context): Promise<() => void> =>
111	  Promise.resolve(ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install))

/**
 * The escalation vocabulary and choreography shared by every sandbox-enforcing
 * tool family (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs`): the
 * strictly-wider ladder, the argument-pairing validation, the model-facing
 * denial/hint markers, and {@link approveEscalation} — the ordered fail-closed
 * sequence that resolves a `sandbox_permissions` request through a
 * user-approval channel BEFORE anything executes. One home keeps the two
 * families' approval ordering and verbatim error texts from drifting apart.
 *
 * The channel is a minimal STRUCTURAL function shape ({@link EscalationAsk}),
 * not the approval service type: the tool layer — which owns the agent, the
 * call id, and the tool name — closes over `ctx.approval.request(...)` and
 * hands the closure down, so this package never depends on the approval or
 * agent packages.
 *
 * @module dsh-sandbox/escalation
 */

import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
import type { SandboxMode } from './index.ts'

/**
 * The strictly-wider table: what a call whose effective mode is the key may
 * escalate TO. Checked at EXECUTION, never baked into a tool schema — the
 * schema's enum is {@link ESCALATION_TARGETS}, because schemas are
 * registry-global while the effective mode is per-call truth.
 */
export const WIDER_MODES: Record<string, readonly SandboxMode[]> = {
  'read-only': ['workspace-write', 'danger-full-access'],
  'workspace-write': ['danger-full-access'],
}

/**
 * The closed escalation-target vocabulary — every mode a call could ever
 * escalate TO (`read-only` is the floor; nothing escalates to it). Advertised
 * whenever the mounted capability confines: cutting the enum down to the modes
 * wider than the composition's DEFAULT would strand a session whose effective
 * mode sits below it (a `danger-full-access` default would advertise nothing
 * while a narrower-switched session stays confined with no lever).
 */
export const ESCALATION_TARGETS: readonly SandboxMode[] = ['workspace-write', 'danger-full-access']

/**
 * Validate the escalation argument pairing a tool schema cannot express:
 * `sandbox_permissions` and `justification` travel together — an approval
 * prompt without a reason, or a reason driving nothing, is a malformed ask —
 * and the justification must be a non-empty sentence.
 * @param sandboxPermissions - the raw `sandbox_permissions` argument, if given.
 * @param justification - the raw `justification` argument, if given.
 */
export function validateEscalationArgs(sandboxPermissions: string | undefined, justification: string | undefined): void {
  if (sandboxPermissions !== undefined && justification === undefined) {
    throw new Error('invalid escalation: sandbox_permissions requires a justification')
  }
  if (justification !== undefined && sandboxPermissions === undefined) {
    throw new Error('invalid escalation: justification is only valid together with sandbox_permissions')
  }
  if (justification !== undefined && justification.trim().length === 0) {
    throw new Error('invalid justification: expected a non-empty sentence')
  }
}

 * The model-facing denial marker — the one vocabulary both enforcing families

 * @param mode - the mode the denied call ran under.
 * @returns the marker line, exactly as the model sees it.
 */
export function sandboxDenialMarker(mode: SandboxMode): string {
  return `[sandbox: file access denied under ${mode} mode]`
}

170	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
171	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
172	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted

175	/** Keep the tail of longer text inside the bound, marking what was dropped. */
176	function bounded(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
177	  return text.length <= maxChars ? text : `…${text.slice(text.length - maxChars + 1)}`
178	}

180	/** Render one executed command's outcome: the exit fact, then whatever it wrote. */
181	function outcomeOf(result: ShellRunResult): string {
182	  const exit = result.exitCode === null
183	    ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}`
184	    : `exit ${String(result.exitCode)}`
185	  const written = [result.stdout.text, result.stderr.text]
186	    .map(stream => stream.trim())
187	    .filter(stream => stream !== '')
188	    .join('\n')
189	  return written === '' ? exit : `${exit}\n${written}`
190	}

252	  /**

254	   *
255	   * The spec is frozen into a digest before anything runs, so starting the same

257	   * ledger instead of forking a second one.
258	   * @param spec - the deliverable to run.

262	   */
263	  async start(spec: ProgramSpec): Promise<ProgramReport> {
264	    const frozen = resolveProgramSpec(spec)
265	    if (!PROGRAM_REVISION.test(frozen.baseRevision)) {
266	      throw new ProgramError(`baseRevision "${frozen.baseRevision}" is not a revision the composed shell can carry unquoted`, 'PROGRAM_INVALID_SPEC')

370	  /** Start a program that has no session yet, or reconcile the one it already has. */
371	  private async open(programId: ProgramId, spec: ProgramSpec): Promise<ProgramReport> {
372	    const scan = await this.scan()
373	    const existing = scan.ledgers.find(ledger => ledger.start.programId === programId)
374	    if (existing !== undefined) {
375	      if (existing.end !== undefined) return this.finishedReport(existing)
376	      return await this.pickUp(existing, scan.sessions)
377	    }
378	    const session = this.ctx.sessions.prepare(SessionId(programId), { meta: { cwd: this.config.workspaceRoot } })
379	    return await this.publish(session, async () => {
380	      session.append('program/start', {
381	        programId,
382	        specSha256: programSpecDigest(spec),
383	        spec,
384	        baseRevision: spec.baseRevision,
385	        ...spec.signoff === undefined ? {} : { signoff: spec.signoff },
386	      })
387	      const run = this.newRun(programId, spec, session)
388	      for (const state of run.states.values()) this.record(run, state)
389	      await this.ctx.sessions.flush(session)
390	      return await this.drive(run)
391	    })
392	  }

394	  /** Reconcile one existing program from its departments and carry it on. */
395	  private async pickUp(ledger: ProgramLedger, sessions: ReadonlyMap<SessionId, ScannedSession>): Promise<ProgramReport> {
396	    const preparation = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.prepare(ledger.sessionId)
397	    try {
398	      return await this.publish(preparation.session, async () => {
399	        const run = this.newRun(ledger.start.programId, ledger.start.spec, preparation.session)
400	        run.integration = ledger.integration
401	        for (const state of run.states.values()) {
402	          const recorded = ledger.goals.get(state.goal.key)
403	          if (recorded !== undefined) {
404	            state.status = recorded.status
405	            state.sessionId = recorded.sessionId
406	            state.workspace = recorded.workspace
407	            state.revision = recorded.revision
408	            state.reason = recorded.reason
409	          }
410	          const reconciled = await this.reconcile(run, state, sessions)
411	          // A goal the ledger never recorded is declared here as well, so a
412	          // ledger written by a process that died mid-declaration still states
413	          // every goal of the spec before it states what became of any of them.
414	          if (recorded === undefined || reconciled) this.record(run, state)
415	        }
416	        preparation.session.append('program/resume', {
417	          programId: run.programId,
418	          statuses: countStatuses([...run.states.values()].map(state => state.status)),
419	        })
420	        await this.ctx.sessions.flush(preparation.session)
421	        return await this.drive(run)
422	      })
423	    } finally {
424	      preparation[Symbol.dispose]()
425	    }
426	  }
